criteria.rationale: The delete_expired method incorrectly calculates the retention period from draft_timestamp instead of receipt_timestamp. Line 43 uses 'notice.draft_timestamp + RETENTION_PERIOD <= now' to determine expiration. The legal requirement specifies that the 7-day retention period must begin at receipt (when the receipt timestamp is recorded), not when the notice is drafted. This means records could be deleted before 7 days from their receipt timestamp if the draft timestamp is earlier than the receipt timestamp.

The notice text and receipt timestamp are stored together in a single Notice dataclass (frozen=True) and in a single database table row. The Notice dataclass (lines 9-15) defines both notice_text and receipt_timestamp as fields of the same immutable object. The database schema stores both columns in the same notices table row with a shared primary key. The receive method creates them together, and there is no code that separates or independently deletes these fields. The association is maintained throughout the retention period.

The notice text is preserved without modification. The receive method accepts notice_text as a parameter and stores it directly in the immutable Notice dataclass without any transformation, sanitization, or removal of content. The database schema defines notice_text as TEXT NOT NULL with no constraints that would strip content. A comprehensive search found no code that modifies, sanitizes, strips, replaces, or removes any part of the notice text, including limiting language. The text flows from input to storage unchanged.
